questions.q: Which bank account is enabled for electronic payment file transmission, and why does this lesson flag that detail?
options: Royal Bank of Canada ...4420, because Canadian payments are always electronic
Regions Bank ...7734, because Chapter 2's supplier EFT payments go out from it and it matters again in bank reconciliation
Both accounts equally, with no particular significance
Neither account supports electronic payments in this design
questions.explain: Regions Bank's ...7734 account is enabled for EFT transmission, which matters again when Chapter 2's bank reconciliation lesson loads the January statement.

questions.q: How many fixed asset categories are configured, and what varies meaningfully across them?
options: Two categories, varying only by currency
Five categories, each with a different useful life
Five categories, all sharing the same 10-year useful life
Three categories, varying by legal entity only
questions.explain: Five categories are configured — Manufacturing Equipment, Office Equipment, Computer Equipment, Furniture & Fixtures, and Building & Leasehold Improvements — each with a different useful life (10, 5, 3, 7, and 15 years respectively).

questions.q: Which two asset categories does this lesson specifically say to keep in mind for later chapters?
options: Computer Equipment and Buildings
Furniture & Fixtures and Computer Equipment
Manufacturing Equipment and Office Equipment
Buildings and Furniture & Fixtures
questions.explain: Manufacturing Equipment (10-year) and Office Equipment (5-year) are flagged because the gap between their useful lives becomes one of Chapter 3's planted problems.

questions.q: How many asset books are configured, and why?
options: One shared asset book for both entities
Two asset books, one per legal entity, consistent with the rest of the enterprise structure
Five asset books, one per category
No asset books are needed until Chapter 3
questions.explain: LTV US Corporate Book and LTV Canada Corporate Book are configured, one per legal entity, following the same per-entity pattern used throughout Chapter 1.

questions.q: What does completing this lesson mark for the capstone overall?
options: The end of the entire capstone
The halfway point of Chapter 3
The completion of Chapter 1's configuration, with Chapter 2 about to begin with real transactions
The start of the final presentation
questions.explain: This lesson closes out Chapter 1's full configuration; Chapter 2 begins next with lesson 9, running real transactions through the structure just built.
